scenario_distribution_note: Development and Holdout are drawn from the identical ScenarioSpace (same target-count range, service-time range, and failure probability -- see internal/tuning/scenario.go's DefaultScenarioSpace), differing only in seed range. This experiment tests generalization to unseen SAMPLES from the same generating distribution, not to a distributionally different traffic shape; it says nothing about robustness under distribution shift, which is what the hand-crafted challenge suite (008-F) probes instead.
holdout_touch_note: Holdout was scored twice across this stage's lifetime: once under the original (p99-based) objective, and again here under the corrected (mean-latency-based) objective after the objective function itself was found to be flawed (see docs/learning/008-tuning-final-validation.md). The correction was motivated entirely by Development-side evidence (008-F's contradictory ranking and the p99/median mismatch found while investigating it) -- Holdout numbers were never inspected or compared before the objective was corrected, so this was not a case of adjusting the method after seeing a disappointing Holdout result. Recorded explicitly because master context rule 9 asks for any re-touching of Holdout to be stated honestly rather than left implicit.
evidence_tier: suggestive: improved on both sets with a small pooled generalization gap, but its 95% bootstrap CI includes zero -- not distinguishable from no gap at this scenario-set size
findings: 008-B's winning candidate (Development utility 0.7191, a 0.0216 improvement over the hand-chosen baseline's 0.6975) was evaluated against the 20-scenario Holdout set for the first and only time. Its Holdout utility was 0.6947 against the baseline's 0.6837 Holdout utility -- a holdout improvement of +0.0110, against a training improvement of +0.0216, for a generalization gap of +0.0106, whose 95% bootstrap CI (per-scenario paired, 5000 resamples) is [-0.0020, 0.0148] (excludes zero: false). Looking past the pooled aggregate: the winner's per-scenario utility distribution on Holdout was mean=0.7167/median=0.7116/worst=0.5710/stddev=0.0839 versus the baseline's mean=0.7026/median=0.7001/worst=0.5751/stddev=0.0748 -- a worst-case regression of -0.0041. Evidence tier: suggestive: improved on both sets with a small pooled generalization gap, but its 95% bootstrap CI includes zero -- not distinguishable from no gap at this scenario-set size.
